plants.name: Rhododendron catawbiense
plants.description: Rounded, evergreen shrubs cover high Appalachian ridges and balds with big clusters of rose-lavender, bell-shaped blooms. They sit against glossy, leathery leaves. In peak season whole hillsides look as if they have been washed in soft purple.
plants.location: Higher slopes, ridges and balds of the southern Appalachian Mountains, eastern United States
plants.funFact: Many of today's hardy garden rhododendrons descend from this native mountain species. Breeders prize it for its tolerance of cold winters.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Peonies have lush, fragrant, bowl-shaped flowers with silky petals, in single, semi-double or fully double forms. They sit atop sturdy stems and deep green, glossy foliage. Gardeners wait for them each year because the show is brief and generous.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring, peaking around late May in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Tibet and China. Widely grown in temperate gardens across North America, Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: A peony can live and flower in the same spot for decades. The plant dies back to the ground each winter and regrows from underground buds every spring.
